cards.title: When Your Child Starts to Stutter
cards.body: A parent's perception of themselves can completely change when their child faces communication challenges. Despite initial feelings of ambivalence, being present for your child during difficult moments matters more than you realize.

cards.title: Navigating Feelings for Your Child's Teacher
cards.body: Crushes can feel freeing because they operate outside everyday life, but acting on them requires careful consideration. As a parent, this situation demands prioritizing your family's wellbeing and school relationships.

cards.title: Maternity Care Access and Safety
cards.body: A two-tier maternity system creates inequality in how safe and supported mothers feel during birth. Universal state care is gradually replacing private systems, though resistance remains from established interests.

cards.title: Music Festivals with Young Children
cards.body: Families bring genuine magic to music festivals, despite criticism from those without children. Parenting twins while attending events reveals how enriching shared experiences can be for families.

cards.title: Can a Stepparent Buy Love?
cards.body: Research shows that a stepparent's generosity can contribute to more positive relationships with stepchildren. Financial support and care are meaningful tools in building family bonds.

cards.title: Before You Judge the Helicopter Mom
cards.body: Contextual factors add crucial nuance to blanket judgments made about helicopter parenting. Understanding the circumstances behind parenting choices leads to more compassionate perspectives.

cards.title: When Teens Hide Self-Harm from Adults
cards.body: Many teens view telling an adult about a friend's self-harm as betrayal rather than help. This concerning attitude can be shifted before it matters through education and cultural change.

cards.title: The 10 Minutes After Your Child Loses It
cards.body: The moment your child finally calms down is when most parents accidentally make things worse. How you respond during this critical window shapes the outcome of emotional crises.

cards.title: Practical Tools for Traumatized Children
cards.body: Adopted and foster children often have exceptional emotional needs requiring specialized approaches. Dr. Karyn Purvis and Lisa Qualls provide strategies for addressing these needs calmly and respectfully.

cards.title: Are You Calling Your College Freshman Too Much?
cards.body: Millions of parents struggle to stay connected with college-bound kids without becoming overbearing. These evidence-based guidelines help parents maintain healthy relationships while respecting their child's independence.

cards.title: Childhood Obesity and School Attendance
cards.body: At specialist childhood obesity clinics, most children are not regularly attending school. This overlooked connection reveals how school absenteeism contributes to the obesity crisis.

cards.title: Forced Adoption Scandal Exposes State Abuse
cards.body: Women were forced by the state to give up their newborns in a shocking British scandal. The full scale of this adoption injustice has finally been revealed and investigated.
